notes.title: v1.0.98
notes.notes:
Honeymoon update!

You may have noticed I've been unusually busy these past few days. It's because I got married! Planning everything was almost as stressful as releasing a game :D

I'm leaving on my honeymoon for a week, but I wanted to leave you with a little gift! (As I typically do before every vacation). Hopefully this time it won't introduce game breaking bugs :)

There is now a new custom map, the Mediterranean! It has 2 different versions, with 21 and 43 cities! The 21 version should feel a bit more like the original game, while the 43 is a bit more jumbo sized, waiting for you guys to build hundreds of businesses and tens of thousands of pops.

Thanks everyone for all the support and kind words so far, see you in a week!

Happy trading,
Lexy.

notes.title: Shops & Mayor Power!
notes.notes: [h3]Mayors[/h3][p]Mayors in High Seas, High Profits! have been a powerful tool towards becoming respected, profiting and expanding your operations in cities, especially in the early-mid game. Their standard features were fairly solid, but it was clear they can be brought to life a bit more.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44879008/0f6804db1e168facd71115244e2c6050e4f3739c.png"][/img][/p][p]The 1st game changer is that now, [b]mayors can fill in their quests on their own[/b], over time. You can still contribute to these quests, and can have a bigger impact than the mayor himself! Manipulating goal orders becomes so much more powerful since mayors will complete their goals in order.[/p][p]With this change, even remote cities have a chance to improve and become more lively. The one goal that mayors can't quite achieve on their own is expanding the city size, as this is quite a big task, requiring donations and the collection of more and more stone.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44879008/a255f6d5d9cf54938985d0f3038f571ad8e337ee.png"][/img][/p][p]Ah, what about choosing your mayor? That's also possible now! A new quest has been added where you can cast your vote for the best mayor to rule the city. Your growing reputation has more and more weight in the city's future, so take a minute to learn about mayor types & vote for the best man for the job![/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44879008/e663551758cb5855cf486db5885552d325763fb9.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][h3]Storage[/h3][p]Storage in High Seas has been a bit of a mini-game in itself. Some move goods around on their ships simply so they don't have to pay rent. Getting storage without renting it was difficult: you had to build more businesses (which end up producing goods anyway). There are now 3 new tools to help you tackle this issue.[/p][p]1. Prices for rented space are now halved! Spicying up the meta a little bit, I'd like to see more central-hub playstyles developing. Lower costs for rented space should allow players to have some items lingering around without breaking bank. In the future, we'll compensate this lowered price with something else (probably increased sailing costs 😈 )[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44879008/8d9972d4ab501924f368b69fb2f7eb6680e1c3f9.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]2. Shops now give a cargo storage allowance. Since they have their own needs, it's more than fair that shops should contribute their fair amount of storage to your warehouse. More storage![/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44879008/797595a695e780a2e51b2700d04be38369e681ef.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]3. There is now a new, HIGHLY anticipated building: the Warehouse! Available through the building menu, the warehouse gives out a flat storage allowance for a monthly cost. You'll still have to strategize around whether the monthly cost is worth it, or you'd rather just rent the space, but this new building still brings in heavy discounts to storage cost, especially in cities where you have tons of goods.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44879008/55bfac06df690c9187f2a1288636e826378486f3.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][h3]Shops[/h3][p]I mentioned them above, but also wanted to have a dedicated section for them. Shops are here![/p][p]Ever felt like the world's not absorbing your pottery quickly enough? The new shops have your back! These new city-owned businesses will allow you to become a manager in someone else's business, supply it with goods and collect the profits![/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44879008/18b94ae1176f672243b6f8d1bb4e16cb31d325a2.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]There's 7 of them and they each have their own needed input goods. Strategically competing for them & providing them with everything that's needed will be a source of great profit, as well as continuous reputation gains. Say bye-bye to 'Not enough reputation'.[/p][p]There's another interesting advantage you get with shops: you don't need to manage employees at all, there's always someone at the counter. Use that wisely.[/p][p]Oh, have I mentioned you won't be the only one managing the shops? AI traders are perfectly capable (and willing) to do it themselves![/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44879008/86d30ad5008ad25ba69e6251fc4a1816fe85f10e.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]You'll have to take care of your shop and supply it with needed goods often, otherwise you'll end up having a heart-to-heart with the mayor.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44879008/d8922b03d7e6c1b0fd1be2e3cc4e86244183c979.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][h3]Auctions[/h3][p]If you don't own the Shop, you're surely wondering how you end up building & managing it? Mayors now have new quests to build these Shops! You can help them or let them figure it out themselves.[/p][p]Once a Shop is built, you can join an auction for its management (provided you have enough reputation).[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44879008/68fcbc2d9d8b79f2cd6b310812b8674e36b779dc.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]Be aware: AI traders will always try to get their sneaky hands on these shops too! it's essential that you get your prices straight, learn how they bid & let some of these 'opportunities' slip.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44879008/db22b9b7b36ca3da1d418b85b32104914eee85e2.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][h3]Lastly[/h3][p]It's been a crazy fun month working on all of this. I've had so much great feedback from people in the Discord ( [url="https://discord.gg/7sKhteQv4w"]https://discord.gg/7sKhteQv4w[/url] ), and that's actually translated in many tinier features![/p][p]Work continues on the few remaining loose ends. Next month I'll share a bit of the new UI. I think it's absolutelly nuts. You'll see soon.[/p][p][/p][p]Until next time,[/p][p]Happy trading![/p][p][/p][p]Lexy.[/p]

notes.title: v1.0.95
notes.notes:
Features:
* there is now a custom quest after completing a warehouse, not the standard new business one.
* the consumption tab of the trader's hall now also takes into consideration your shops
* winter mode can now be disabled completely when starting a new game
* you can now set a new price for a good when selling / buying for all trade routes AND all warehouses from the convoy automatic trade helper.
* you can now see all your shops in a list similar to the businesses list
* successfully supplying a shop will now grant additional reputation
* you can now lose your shop if you neglect it for too long (not your own businesses, those are safe)
* there is now a quest to notify you of a shop that has been neglected and could soon be seized
* after losing a shop, an auction is now created for its management. While you're no longer explicitly invited, you can still participate in the auction.
* AI traders can now lose management of their shops. It's random & the chance is low, but it still happens quite often, especially if there are many shops in your world.
* mayors no longer work on the goal to expand the city on their own. That's something you'll need to help them with.
* you will now lose part of your reputation in a city if you lose a shop.
* player reputation is now directly visible in the world view for any discovered city

Bugs:
* shops would sometimes sell less goods than planned.
* the consumption shown in the trader's hall would not take into consideration businesses missing resources
* it was possible to sometimes crash the convoy statistics window when changing the currently viewed trading session.
* an error was thrown when you were in the ship sale window and the ship is taken away because it's in fact temporarily rented.

notes.title: v1.0.84
notes.notes:
New features:
* new warning system! It will draw your attention if you have businesses that have halted production because you need input goods, if you're attacked by pirates, if you have broken ships, etc. Please send me more ideas on what kind of warnings you'd like to see in the game!
* new error collection system! Errors and crashes are now logged and sent to the server. None of the data colected is personal or can be linked back to players. You can turn off the system entirely in the settings.

Bugfixes:

* hovering a city on the world map did not play a sound

notes.title: Convoy Statistics!
notes.notes: [h3]Set it and forget it?[/h3][p]Automated convoys are one of the most powerful wealth-building tools in-game. They allow for a bunch of different strategies. Collect goods from all of your businesses in 1 or several hubs (then distribute them to surrounding cities), straight up carry everything on your back, and haggle throughout the world or anything in between![/p][p]One of the problems with convoys has been that after creating your route, you were a bit in the dark in regards to exactly what happened while they were trading. That stops today![/p][p][/p][h3]Granularity first[/h3][p]The new system registers up to 11 trading runs, with each one of them ending after the last city on your list is visited. In these runs, you can see where the convoy has stopped, what goods were bought, sold, loaded and unloaded, how the total cargo capacity changed, etc.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44879008/874db92d3c94e22a2b5effcc71b3d88c8f2066a0.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]You can even filter your view to only include 1 single good! Moreover, you're only shown goods that have actually been traded in that run. This will help you debug your routes and ensure you buy/load exactly what you need and sell as much as possible, for the best prices![/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44879008/dc11178c6fa5a8dbd0d2c0e77c5dea6181555694.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]Here's an example: I have a route where I buy every single production bonus good from every city I visit, and then try to sell them everything else. [/p][p]Here's what I mean:[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44879008/0a0f7f58056f3dd18db9ceefc9133a3a443675a9.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]Here's how I've been doing in my latest run on Iron bars:[/p][p]Bought:[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44879008/13f822b7663b2fd524e2d704660c0051b08587b6.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]Sold:[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44879008/1f85338acd338b8783c2040eb8f6de122145b2eb.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]As you can see, I managed to load up on 10 bars on this run (in Pellin and Alemstra), and sold all of them by the end (and an extra 4 crates that I picked in a previous run!). Pair this info with my convoy's hold having no more bars, it's a pretty good indication that there's good demand right now! I might increase the prices a little bit or pick up more bars to further increase my profit.[/p][p]What about available cargo space?[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44879008/dd8e81cdc40d6a27c8659a93ab4c50b344200491.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]My convoy has about 650 total cargo capacity, and the max I reached in this run is 368. I'm good for now, I don't need to add any more ships in, I could even pull a tinier ship or 2 into some other convoy![/p][p][/p][h3]What is profit after all?[/h3][p]You might notice there's a couple of different ways profit is presented. That's because you can look at profit in different ways! [/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44879008/5bb4bdc8d709e3222c8173c4d5a63fb2ba5e9c9d.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]If you just look at all of our income and spending, that's the simplest way to consider profit! We sold stuff, bought more and then repaired our ships. Simple enough, right?[/p][p]Well, what happens with goods you already had on your ship? What about those loaded or unloaded in different ports? Deciding on profit for those is more complicated. [/p][p]The 2nd profit formula looks at individual sales and what cost you to get that product. Say you had 10 crates of Iron Bars on your ship and got those for 185 coins per crate. When you sell them, the profit (or loss!) will be tracked. Adding the profit from every single transaction (and subtracting ship repairs) gets you the 2nd profit type![/p][p]In the example above, the simple profit is lower. That's because we loaded up on some goods that we didn't sell! We'll sell them eventually & then the simple profit will be higher![/p][p][/p][h3]More convoy updates?[/h3][p]Yes! But after the new UI gets implemented. There's still a lot of stuff that's too complicated, especially when setting up trade routes. I think you'll love the new UI. I actually started working on its design. Leave a comment if you'd like a sneak peek, or would prefer to be surprised.[/p][p][/p][p]Until next time,[/p][p]Happy trading.[/p][p]Lexy.[/p]

notes.title: v1.0.79
notes.notes:
Bugfix:
- winter would sometimes fail to end :(

Quality of life:
- you can now choose which difficulty modifiers you would like to play with. If you don't like one in particular, you can turn it off.
- added a new option to Prevent ports from freezing during winter.
- there is now a hotkey to Focus the selected ship in world view.

notes.title: v1.0.77
notes.notes:
Many tiny QoL updates
- there is now a warning (in the build window) when you have insufficient reputation to build.
- hovering over the warning also gives extra information about reputation tiers and how much you can build for each one of them.
- moved reputation information from Traders Hall to Town Hall in preparation for more details being added.
- there is now a bit more info about reputation in the town's hall.
- mayors will now no longer give a flat rate for goods sold as part of a quest. Instead, if a city has a lot of cheap goods, the mayor will also offer the same price as buying from the market directly.
- updated screenshots of ships in the Shipyard build menu so it contains the new sea.
- moved info about ship type and made it bigger.
- there is now a list of the most recent 10 seeds you've played in your games and the starter cities for each one of them, so you can more easily find the right one.
- every list allowing a file to be loaded or saved will now also allow you to double click to load / double click to save in addition to clicking an item and then clicking the load / save button.
- there is now a confirmation window when making a new save with the same name as an existing one (e.g. overriding the existing save).
- you can now set up keymaps to quickly select your ships!
- tooltips for city production and consumption now clearly specify this is monthly production / consumption.
- you can now drag the world and city maps around by clicking the ground. Can be disabled in settings.
- you can now temporarily disable the price guard until you close the trade window. It will allow you to do 'bad' trades for strategic reasons, but only until you close the trading window and open it again.
- I've adjusted some ship characteristics: Skiffs now need an extra sailor (6 instead of 5). Caravels and Carracks now have way larger cargo holds but also need considerably more materials to be built.
- the new business window now shows production with city bonus included, as well as information about the base production for cities having a specific bonus.
- winter production is now also shown during the summer, to allow a more informed decision.

Bugs:
- winter production would not be shown correctly in the UI
- after creating a new game with a custom map, if you loaded an existing save with a different custom map, the world generation would get confused and load in the wrong terrain.

notes.title: Winter is here!
notes.notes: [h3]Winter is here![/h3][p]If there's one thing a high sea trader loves, that's opportunities for profit! Winter is definitelly one of them.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44879008/42e913810e92e2e7876452a7c3995dc8ebddeee2.png"][/img][/p][p]Jump in and discover some goods that have reduced production during winter & the impact that has on consumption, pop happiness and your own businesses![/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44879008/5eadf2dbe14ddcb740ef00b6584c3f4f15df2698.png"][/img][/p][h3]All smooth sailing, right?[/h3][p]There's never a free meal, capturing these new opportunities comes at a cost: plan around ports freezing, ensure your supply chains are up to date and there's enough stock to pass a long winter. Or just risk everything, hope for a short winter and dump as much grain into cities as humanly possible! It's up to you.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44879008/f8eb29ccedfaf92d539faff645c7703d2e368d49.png"][/img][/p][h3]Smarter convoys[/h3][p]New options have been added to allow you to instruct your automated convoys on how to act around frozen ports.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44879008/2de3af5a1521ca2fb22546a2f794761136f813b4.png"][/img][/p][p]There's a few more effects / QoL updates that will roll out soon impacting winter mode. There might even be some difficulty modifiers targetting the new season.[/p][p][/p][p]Please give it a shot and let me know how it feels![/p][p][/p][p]Happy trading,[/p][p]Lexy.[/p][p][/p][p][/p]

notes.title: Roadmap!
notes.notes:
As some of you might know, I've been on an epic month-long vacation. It's a first for me, and it has been incredible. The time of vacation-ing has ended. The time of building is now upon us!

In this post I'll present the game's Roadmap. It's a pretty long read. Strap in!

[h3]Loose ends (June-July)[/h3]
There are many tinier features that were planned, but deprioritized for the release. There were other, more important things that needed to be in the game. It’s now the time to tie all these loose ends.
[list]
[*] remaining difficulty modifiers
[*] winter mode!
[*] big list of QoL features
[*] rebalancing ships perks + pirate encounters
[*] trade routes: statistics + more advanced management tools
[*] mayors: election process, player managed city-owned shops, auctions, more mayor quests
[*] notification / warning system for broken ships, businesses missing resources, pirate attacks, etc.
[*] ship customization
[*] the Sarnis campaign (FINALLY!)
[*] mark campaigns as completed (major oversight, sorries)
[*] free-play goals
[*] new warehouse building
[/list]
[h3]New UI + localization (July - September)[/h3]
The most consistent complaint I’ve seen is that the font is hard to read. You’re absolutely right. Additionally, the biggest feature request (BY FAR) I’ve received is support for other languages. These 2 areas are actually connected. The font that the game uses won’t allow a bunch of the characters that other languages need. If we also add in all the awesome feedback you gave about what the current UI does terribly, we have ourselves a full UI-centric update!
[list]
[*] new UI system that’s cleaner, has a better font & nicer overall aesthetic
[*] improve many of the windows (looking at you trading window, buy 1, buy 5 shenanigans)
[*] more tools to manage fleets, trading routes, global inventory view & upgrades
[*] localization for the first language set: german, spanish, french, russian
[/list]
[h3]The sandbox (September - November)[/h3]
It’s no secret that the biggest inspiration for High Seas has been Patrician 3. I just love that game. I do however want High Seas to also further develop its own identity. I always felt that with the procedural map, this game is a bit more open to a sandboxy environment. Moving forward, I want to lean a bit more into that.
[list]
[*] fully featured map editor with a land painting tool, allowing the exact placement of cities and hand-crafting economies, setting up goals.
[*] steam workshop integration so that you can share your custom games + find new, interesting ones.
[/list]
[h3]The future (November +)[/h3]
I will always be adding more and more things I find fun to the game. Reality is however, I won’t always be able to dedicate my full focus to it. At some point I will prototype some more cool games, and I hope you guys will be along for the ride!
[list]
[*] improve robot trader AI: robot traders will have goals, build their own businesses and more ships, allowing for a more immersive world, as well as making strategic use of them.
[*] v1 of mod support, probably in the shape of a demo mod, allowing new buildings, ships, UIs and hooking into the game’s event system
[*] a bunch of other stuff I have probably promised but am forgetting right now.
[/list]
[h3]Maybe-land (2026 - 2099)[/h3]
These are all random ideas and hard to implement features that people would like to see in the game. I would also love to have them! No promises though.
[list]
[*] extract the game core and open source it
[*] use the game core as a server and package it with the visual client, in order toooooo
[*] allow multiplayer
[*] add a pirate combat minigame (and becoming a pirate ofc!)
[*] church focused free DLC with new buildings, quests, economies and more stats to track!
[*] politics focused free DLC allowing you to influence elections or become the actual mayor
[*] community crowdsourced localizations for other languages or even a system to load localization packs from the workshop
[*] female captains & mayors
[/list]
[h3]Goodies (all the time!)[/h3]
Some of the updates above will be slow. I want to give you guys something fresh to try out from time to time! That’s where the goodies come in!
[list]
[*] more custom maps before the map editor is released (in fact, I have one in the works right now, and it has a crazy amount of cities in it)
[*] improved captains - be able to find captains in special places, earn them through quests or remove bad traits from existing ones. I also heard rumors about some kind of academy…
[*] creating new settlements
[*] building dwellings and becoming a landlord
[*] more quests! in fact as soon as we have at least a decent pool of them, I should be able to re-enable quests in the free play since they won’t be as repetitive anymore. Keep a look out in the Discord for some kind of quest-creation competition
[*] more campaigns!
[*] more achievements
[*] more city sizes (larger cities)
[/list]
[h3]Lastly[/h3]
I plan to start a let’s play series on Youtube! I am not a Youtuber and Lord knows how consistent I’ll be with actually uploading, but I’d love to do at least a 30min - 1h episode a week. I think it could be cool to see how I imagined playing the game, as I’m sure everyone will have their very own style. The channel's here https://www.youtube.com/@lexydotzip although I haven't uploaded anything to it in 4 months, and it has a grand total of 38 subs :)

Thanks so much for all your support & your patience during my vacation! Please keep the awesome feedback and suggestions coming in either the feedback form or the Discord!

Happy trading!
Lexy.

notes.title: High Seas, High Profits! devlog #5
notes.notes:
Hello world!

It’s been a while since the last devlog, but for good reason! I’ve been doing more than stuffing my face with cozonac and sarmale (delicious romanian foods), albeit there was plenty of that too. Today we’re going to look at all the most recent developments: the new economy & reputation systems, the ability to switch between RTS and TBS, the new graphics, the beta challenge, and the launch of the public demo!

[h3]It’s not always 3 sacks of grain for a barrel of wine[/h3]

High Seas was always meant to have a dynamic pricing system where prices for different goods differ both depending on cities (different stock, consumption and production rates) as well as your game’s seed. Different games, different prices! Previously, this was accomplished by having a core price for a good and then using the game seed to adjust that with a multiplier between 0.5x and 2x. Say if wine’s core price was 100 coins, you’d never get a game where the production cost of wine was outside the range 50-200. This worked, but it made prices fairly similar, they would in some sense clump together. Moreover, costs of producing things could be desynced from the price cities would buy / sell goods for. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44879008/b5498ce4cc91b799444815d8b7523e9cce08bc0d.png[/img]

The new economy system ties things together. The 21 goods have been split between 3 buckets, depending on what kind of pops they require to produce. Within the buckets, there are 7 pricing tiers. Through some slightly complex math (I only dare say ‘slightly’ now since it’s done, it did not seem that way when I first had to do it) the bucket, tier and seed lead to a new concept called base production cost. That’s basically what the good would cost to produce if no bonuses would be involved and any input goods would also be purchased at base production cost. Through this we can now calculate many things: what cities are willing to pay for goods when they need it & what they want for them when they sell them, what you have to pay your workers to produce goods, etc.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44879008/e829cad38bc28efebc021947596a30d1b29b37c6.png[/img]

Overall the new economy seems a lot more fair & producing goods has a bit more predictability. It’s also now more apparent that some businesses become people-centric while others are input-good heavy. Depending on your game, which is which will change, and that ads a bit more complexity in understanding what to prioritize throughout the game.

[h3]Button mashing or cocktail sipping[/h3]

A highly-requested feature was the ability to play the game in real time mode. Many players are familiar with the Port Royale series, Patrician 3 and Sid Meier’s: Pirates! These games have been the main inspiration for High Seas as well! One of the things they had in common while High Seas lacked, was that they were real time games. That changes today! In High Seas, High Profits! you can now switch between Real Time and Turn Based mode at any time!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44879008/fb8ad167205507808852c46d36e965e294a09808.gif[/img]

Enjoy a high pace sim with multiple speed levels or switch to TBS and sip on a Martini. Or ale. You can sip on ale, right?

[h3]Power to the people![/h3]

The game’s demo is now public! I always intended for High Seas to have a public demo & limit the demo to some kind of predefined experience + period in time, but not to guard away mechanics. For now, this experience will be the Beta Challenge! This first step guides players through the basic mechanics & helps establish the first business + first convoys. If you want to dig deeper, you can! The sim runs for 4 in-game years, which should be plenty to complete the challenge and get a feel for the game. Two more campaigns will be release soon, giving even more insight into how different mechanics from the game work.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44879008/3faf8f9f89b1970b0031bc4a5346915b1f59116f.png[/img]

[h3]Waves, hills and godrays[/h3]

I’ve been postponing the visual v3 update for a while, but the time for it is now. I love clean, almost vector art aesthetics and I hope I managed to capture that with the most recent changes. I really wanted there to be godrays and I managed to cobble up some pretty cool ones. They could be improved, but they’re still pretty fun.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44879008/aca6fd2e437a07a92ef7cdf7399672bfc724b493.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44879008/53b0f32983871aa83c35cbd81be66d722e8db881.png[/img]

There are a few more visual upgrades I had in mind, but this’ll have to do for now since there are more pressing things at hand.

[h3]I challenge you to a duel! (not really a duel)[/h3]

The beta challenge was meant to be a fun little activity for the Discord community during the closed alpha+beta, but I decided to open it up and give more people a shot. In short: play the game, complete the beta challenges in-game (which acts like a mini-tutorial) and get a chance to win a copy of the game! Moreover, fastest to do it (in-game time) is guaranteed a copy!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44879008/33576faa0dab90baedca16a63ba5c70b7fcf4904.png[/img]

The beta challenge will be improved and become the tutorial soon, so take your shot now, while it’s still active.

Oh, just so I don’t forget - if you ever get stuck during the challenge, fear not! I actually played through the entire challenge, and made a video! Here it is:

[previewyoutube=nnvUfGmEeDc;leftthumb][/previewyoutube]


[h3]This is all on you[/h3]

Lastly, I wanted to thank everyone who’s checked out the game, everyone who’s submitted even the tiniest piece of feedback, everyone who’s ever wishlisted the game. Your thoughts, struggles and awesome ideas have helped this little game grow so much! You’re awesome, and I can’t wait to show you all what I’ve planned next! No spoilers this time.

Happy trading,

Lexy.

notes.title: High Seas, High Profits! devlog #4
notes.notes:
Hello there traveler!
I know you've been awaiting a new devlog for quite some time, but fear not, your wait has ended!

[h3]Alpha is available in Discord[/h3]
It's been a long journey but the alpha is finally in the hands of Discord members. If you haven't joined the Discord, this is probably the best time. You'll be able to grab a key and check out the game today!

Launching the alpha revealed some very interesting facts - there was no way to actually figure out the game. I went by popular internet opinion and didn't add a tutorial since for an alpha that makes less sense (it'll be obsolete soon, etc.), This resulted in very few people knowing how to play the game. One of the first things I therefore had to address was having the game be more intuitive & having a 'Challenge' section which acts as a quick tutorial into how to move around the map, how to trade & build businesses. Moving forward, I'll have to look into adding a kickass tutorial to explain all the game has to offer.

Here's the happy merchant I made for the challenges. A youtuber called him 'little pirate dude' which I thought was funny.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44879008/dffb98b877f675fb7df5f968372a9d30bf3d24d6.png[/img]

[h3]The power of sound![/h3]
Finally, after more than 3 weeks of curating music & sounds, the game now has an ambiance! There's chill medieval music in the background & cities have workers hammering away while dogs bark by the docks. Overall I feel it ads a lot of atmosphere to the environment. It's not perfect, but it's getting there. Adding sounds meant I also needed to add the settings to control them, so I went the extra mile and also added in controls & graphics settings. My french friends should also now be able to play using Azerty keyboards while multi-monitor folks should now be able to move the game around to their heart's content!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44879008/8c1ef0c0fd96dfffadc44910eca2d785922ed5d7.gif[/img]

[h3]Ship upgrades, quality of life, tooltips and so much more[/h3]

Alpha testing has been great & provided me with incredible feedback on so many things that were either not clear, not working or just not at the right level of quality. I've already addressed a ton of them & more will soon hit the alpha!

[h3]Up next[/h3]

I'll probably wrap the session off with visuals v3 - a new graphical update - before the beta release in December.

Thanks for checking out the devlog! Remember to play the alpha if you haven't already (grab a key in discord [url=https://discord.gg/7sKhteQv4w]https://discord.gg/7sKhteQv4w[/url]) and until next time, happy trading!

Lexy.

notes.title: High Seas, High Profits! devlog #3
notes.notes:
Ahoy, aspiring merchant moguls!
Welcome aboard for our third devlog of High Seas, High Profits! I've been as busy as a one-legged pirate in a kickboxing contest, so let's dive right in!

[h3]Tooltip takeover: knowledge is power (and profit!)[/h3]

First up, I've implemented a brand new tooltip system. Now you can hover over various elements in the game to get insights into all the intricate mechanics of trade, city management, and navigation. These tooltips will give you the lowdown on all the cool concepts in the game, ensuring you're never lost at sea when it comes to understanding game mechanics. The tooltip system is inspired by games such as Crusader Kings 3 and Norland.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44879008/5d9c7ef32a48d99f28dcbbbe38ec97ca8caf2db2.png[/img]

[h3]Citizen satisfaction: the foundation of thriving cities[/h3]

I've introduced a happiness system for your city-dwelling populations. Happy citizens are the wind in your sails, affecting everything from migration to consumption, and even influencing world events.
Each social class - poor, middle, and upper - has its own happiness factors. Balancing the needs of all your citizens is as challenging as navigating a ship through a stormy strait, but when done right - just as rewarding. Fear not! The new detailed happiness window shows you exactly what's influencing your citizens' moods.

I've refined how goods are distributed among social classes. It's a delicate economic ballet, ensuring that luxury goods reach the upper class while keeping necessities affordable for all. The system simulates the complex supply and demand dynamics of a bustling medieval port city. Oh, and I also made a video about it:

https://youtu.be/ByO18aTNN1I

[h3]Captains: the real stars of the nautical show[/h3]

Exciting news from the docks - captains have arrived! These experienced sailors will be crucial in managing your expanding trade network. Each captain comes with their own dashing portrait, reflecting the diverse backgrounds of medieval seafarers.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44879008/a5e54c92dc5d16d24f64f94895ecf5ae61043062.png[/img]

But a captain's worth isn't just in their appearance. They come with both positive and negative traits that can significantly impact your trading operations. You might discover a master navigator who can shorten your voyage times, or end up with a poor negotiator who struggles to get the best prices in foreign markets. Don't worry though - you can hire a new captain every 12 turns if your current one isn't meeting your mercantile standards.
I've added 20 traits to start with - 10 positive and 10 negative. Keep an eye out for special traits that can only be earned through quests or other in-game events!

https://youtu.be/xIFykC1gQRE

[h3]On the horizon[/h3]
We're currently charting a course towards ship upgrades. Soon you'll be able to enhance your vessels to better suit your trading strategies!

That's all for now, esteemed traders! Check back soon for more updates.

Join the Discord if you haven't already, I value your input like a merchant values their ledger!

Until next time, happy trading!

- Lexy

notes.title: High Seas, High Profits! devlog #2
notes.notes:
Ahoy, traders and seafarers! Welcome back to another exciting devlog for High Seas, High Profits! Grab your ledgers and quills, because we've got a boatload of updates to share. Let's dive right in!

[h3]The Trader's Hall: Your Medieval Money Machine[/h3]
I've been hard at work on the Trader's Hall, the beating heart of our medieval trading empire. This central hub is where you'll manage your goods & production, and where you chat with other traders. Think of it as a medieval Wall Street, but with more rats and less air conditioning.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44879008/1656f61f7d14bdb5b686f11aeb43e7fa9c6a0363.gif[/img]

The first thing you'll notice is the snazzy new blue flag adorning the hall, complete with a white goods bag icon. I'm so fond of it that you might see flags popping up all over the place soon.

[h3]Five Pillars of Trade: The Trader's Hall Features[/h3]
The Trader's Hall now boasts five key features, each designed to give you full control over your budding trade empire:

[b]The Overview:[/b] This is your one-stop-shop for all things trade-related in your city. Want to know which goods have production bonuses? Curious about city-wide perks? Need a list of traders operating in your turf? The Overview has got you covered.

[b]The Warehouse:[/b] This is where your goods are stored, with businesses providing cargo space. Don't worry about running out of room - the city's got your back with cheap rental space. Unless you're playing on higher difficulty levels, in which case... well, good luck counting those pennies!

[b]Production:[/b] Here's where you can see what both you & the other traders are making in the city.

[b]Consumption:[/b] Keep track of what your city and businesses are eating up. It's sort of like a medieval grocery list.

[b]Trading:[/b] Set up your buy and sell orders, manage your stock limits, and watch as your automated trading empire grows. It's like programming your coffee maker, but for profits!

[previewyoutube=_YeWSeNgFgg;leftthumb][/previewyoutube]


[h3]Production and Consumption: A Delicate Balance[/h3]

Let's talk numbers. I've been wrestling with production values, trying to ensure that 10 sacks of clay don't magically turn into 30 sacks of bricks. It's harder than it sounds - medieval alchemy is tricky business! Did you know it takes 4 people a whole month to mix 6 barrels of wine with 1 barrel of honey and make 7 barrels of mead? I suspect most of that time is 'quality control tasting'.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44879008/a978dce87f847272cc6cfa941d5d9472d6d4505a.png[/img]

I've also implemented a system where production and consumption depend on employed population. Some businesses even require an upper-class pop as a manager. No manager? Your business operates at half capacity. It's like medieval middle management, but with EVEN MORE fancy hats.

In the future you'll be able to save and load order sets, because who wants to manually input "buy low, sell high" for the umpteenth time?

[h3]The Nitty-Gritty: Production and Consumption Cycles[/h3]

Here's how it all comes together:
[list]
[*] Businesses start in a "Needs resources" phase.
[*] The warehouse is checked for available inputs.
[*] If resources are available, they're removed from the warehouse.
[*] Four turns later, voila! Production complete.
[*] Rinse and repeat.
[/list]

The city market acts as a warehouse for NPC traders & city owned businesses. It's like a medieval Amazon fulfillment center, but 'Prime' means you get first pick of the least moldy items.

[previewyoutube=e5X0K95XRR0;leftthumb][/previewyoutube]


[h3]Wrapping Up[/h3]

That's all for now, folks! We've covered trading halls, production cycles, automatic trading, and even touched on medieval wine-mixing techniques. Who said trading simulations couldn't be educational?
Stay tuned for more updates, wishlist if you haven't and until next time, happy trading!

notes.title: High Seas, High Profits! devlog #1
notes.notes:
Hey everyone! Lexy here, I'm excited to share some fantastic updates on our medieval naval trading game. It's been a productive couple of weeks, and I've made significant progress on the building system. Let's dive into the latest developments!

[h3]Building System Overhaul[/h3]
The journey began with creating a new board that bundles together all the cards needed for a fully functional building system. The first feature was the ability for buildings to switch between their built model and the worksite model. Now, every building you place will have an "under construction" mode, adding a layer of realism to your growing cities.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44879008/19336710e2af970ee8323892e8709e3c71d6a078.png[/img]

[h3]Squashing Bugs[/h3]
With new features come new bugs. I encountered an issue where buildings could be placed on top of existing ones. The placement algorithm wasn't checking for existing structures, but that's now fixed. Another bug involved some buildings not being clickable because the ground would intercept the events. That’s sorted too.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44879008/c83129172171c1d973322a9630cd2e4d1cf1c10f.png[/img]

I also fixed a bug where city buildings appeared on the world map, creating a bizarre and unintended sight! And there was an issue where the worksite wasn’t immediately shown after placing a building, plus a flicker effect when entering a city map. All fixed!

[h3]Fine-Tuning the Building Menu[/h3]
The build menu is now much more user-friendly. All build options are correctly linked to their respective details, and I've fixed all the filters. Clicking on "build" will now construct the intended building, not just the default Brewery. Unless you just want Breweries everywhere, which, honestly, I wouldn’t judge.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44879008/21b3b00db60b35f4dcfed1144d8772a9ed261dd8.png[/img]

[h3]Improved Placement Options[/h3]
A new tiny window now allows you to cancel the current building placement and soon will let you rotate buildings during placement. The green shadow/highlight shown during placement will now correctly represent the building model, ensuring you have a clear idea of what you’re placing.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44879008/981287edf15ca2e74b83243489d259ef86e4e348.png[/img]

Moreover, the placement validation algorithm now considers the actual size of buildings, instead of assuming a 3x3 grid. This change enables more complex and visually interesting city layouts.

[h3]Building Rotations and Progress[/h3]
I’ve implemented building rotations! This means you can now rotate your buildings for better city planning and aesthetics. Additionally, I've fixed a bug where the cancel or rotate buttons in the building options UI wouldn't block clicks on the city map, preventing accidental placements.

New buildings now progress through construction phases until they become operational. This adds a dynamic element to city-building, letting you watch your cities grow over time.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44879008/dbb7c85b10281ce0d447d0678cad5bef21a05bdc.gif[/img]

[h3]Population Management[/h3]
The latest major update involves population management. Now, pops (population units) are automatically assigned to new buildings whenever there are unemployed pops available. This ensures that your new businesses will have workers ready to go. However, if the number of employed pops exceeds the total pops in the city, some will be reassigned to balance things out.

[h3]Looking Ahead[/h3]
Now that these features are in place, the core of the building system is nearly finished. Up next, I’ll be fine-tuning the building requirements, costs, and production values to make sure the gameplay is balanced and fun.

Thank you all for your continued support and feedback. It’s your enthusiasm that keeps this project moving forward. Stay tuned for more updates, and happy building!

Cheers,
Lexy
